FOREWORD
by the Indian Standards draft finalized by the Soaps Committee had been appro-

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted Institution on 30 March 1983, after the and Other Surface Active Agents Sectional ved by the Chemical Division Council.

0.2 Castor oil is abundantly available in India and has varied applications. However, because of the very high percentage of hydroxy acids, it is unsuitable for incorporation in fat charges for soap making, except It is, however, possible to chemically in very restricted quantities. treat this oil to reduce and/or remove the hydroxy groups so that the oil contains predominantly stearic and monoene acids and can therefore be used as raw material for soaps to substitute tallow or hardened oils. 0.3 This standard is intended to encourage more manufacturers, not only to make a standard product for captive use, but also to make it available for general use. 0.4 Castor oleine and oleostearine are triglycerides derived from castor oil, chemically treated to eliminate hydroxyl ( OH ) groups of ricinoleic acid. The product shall be oleine or oleostearine depending on the unsaturation in the final product. 0.5 This standard contains clause 4.1 which calls for agreement the purchaser and the supplier. between

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-196O*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )

A-1.5.1 Preparation of 0.5 N Hydroxylmine Hydrochloride Solution Dissolve 39.9 g of recrystallized hydroxylamine hydrochloride in 100 ml of distilled water; warm to a temperature of 650�C on a steam bath to yield a clear solution. Add this solution slowly to 1 000 ml of 95 percent alcohol and mix thoroughly. Then add 50 ml of a 0'1 percent solution of bromophenol blue indicator in 50 percent alcohol and sufficient 0'5 N alcoholic sodium hydroxide solution to a greenish shade; this usually requires about 20 to 25 ml of alkali. B-2. PROCEDURE B-2.1 Preparatiou of Fatty Acids - With the aid of heat, dissolve 40 g of solid potassium hydroxide in 200 g of glycerine. Bring the temperature of the mixture to 150�C and add 100 g of oil or melted fat sample and reheat to 140-150�C. Continue stirring until saponification Cool slightly and add about is complete. Do not heat to above 150�C. 400-500 ml water, stir the mass well and heat until the soap is dissolved. Add carefully while stirring 1CO ml of sulphuric acid ( 50 percent by mass ). Boil until the fatty acids are completely melted and clear. Remove the aqueous layer by siphon, add fresh water and boil again till the fatty acids are clear and melted. Siphon the aqueous layer and repeat washings till the aqueous layer is neutral to methyl orange indicator. Pass the fatty acids through filter paper to dry them. B-2.2 Preparation of Methyl Esters - Reflux the dried fatty acids as obtained in A-2.1 for 2 hours with about 4 times their mass of methyl Distil the alcohol containing 1 percent of concentrated sulphuric acid. unreacted methanol and wash the esters free of mineral acid. B-2.3 Distillation - Weigh accurately about 50 g of the methyl esters as obtained in A-2.2 in a IOO-ml distillation flask. Distil the methyl Weigh the esters at 210�C under a vacuum of l-5 mm of mercury. residue left in the distillation flask. B-3. APPENDIX C [ Table 1, Item (x) ]
DETERMINATION C-O. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD OF NICKEL

C-O.1 The method is based on the isolation of metal from the soap and reaction between nickel in the oxidised form with dimethyl glyoxime forming a red colour, the intensity of which is proportional to the amount of nickel present in the sample. C-l. C-l.1 C-2. C-2.1 C-2.2 APPARATUS UV Spectrophotometer

PROCEDURE

C-3.1 Isolation of Metals from Caster Oleine and Caster Oleostearine - To 40 g of sample in a 500-ml beaker add 40 ml of caustic soda solution containing 8 g of sodium hydroxide; mix well and heat on Add 200 ml hot water, water bath until the saponification is complete. heat until all the soap goes into solution. Add to this soap solution 40 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid, stir and keep on steam bath until fatty acid layer separates. Add 20 g of paraffin wax, stir at intervals Cool to room temperature. and allow to settle until phases are clear. C-3.1.1 Remove wax cake with rod, rinse with water and add rinsings Evaporate aqueous phase to about 60 ml by gentle to aqueous phase. Add 100 ml of water and filter through pap?r washed previboiling. ously with hydrochloric acid. Evaporate the filtrate and washings to about 60 ml. Cool and transfer to volumetric flask. Make up the volume to 100 ml. Take aliquot portions for metal estimation. 9

LS:10536-1983 C-3.2 Determination of Nickel Content - Take 50 ml aliquot of Evapothe aqueous solution from the test solution in a 250-ml beaker. Transfer the solution to a rate the solution to about 15 ml by heating. 50-ml glass stoppered volumetric flask using a small quantity of water for rinsing the solution from the beaker into the volumetric flask. Add to the flask 3 ml of saturated bromine water and allow to stand for one minute. Add ammonia liquor dropwise until excess bromine is destroyed as indicated by the disappearance of brown colour. Then add 5 ml of ammonia liquor in excess. If a precipitation occurs, filter the solution and wash the precipitate with water; combine the filtrate and the washings and concentrate to a volume of a few ml and transfer to a 50-ml volumetric flask. Add 10 ml of dimethyl glyoxime solution, Mix thoroughly and followed by 15-20 ml of 95 percent. ethyl alcohol. make up the volume and again mix thorougly. Allow the solution to stand for 5 minutes to permit full development of colour and take the absorption/transmittance reading at 445 nm. Prepare and conduct blank determination simultaneously and similar in all respects. The transmittance of the blank should be 98 f 1 percent. Determine the nickel content of the sample by reference to a concentration-transmittance graph prepared as follows. C-3.3 Preparation of Concentration Transmittance Graph Weigh accurately 2,261 7 g of nickel sulphate ( 99 percent NiS04*6HsO ) and dissolve in water in a 500-ml volumetric flask. Add 30 ml of concentrated hydrochloric acid and bring to volume. This solution contains 1 000 pg of nickel per ml. Make appropriate dilutions of this solution and process this solution as in sample above. The dilutions should cover a range O-100 pg. Finally plot a curve relating transmittance to micrograms of nickel.
